speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: The National Research Foundation (NRF) seeks to harness science and technology (S&T) to create new opportunities for economic growth in a post-COVID-19 world, and support Singapore's national and societal needs.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: S&T has played a critical role in Singapore's fight against COVID-19.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Public research and development (R&D) institutes, such as the Agency for Science, Technology and Research, worked closely with the public health community in Singapore to develop accurate diagnostic test kits and effective treatment methods.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Our RIE efforts will remain key in enabling Singapore to meet future national challenges, and to create new opportunities for economic growth in a post-COVID-19 world.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Through our RIE plan for the next 5 years, NRF will support basic and applied research in high impact strategic areas, building on our S&T strengths in advanced manufacturing and engineering, health and biomedical sciences, sustainability and urban solutions, as well as digital technologies.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Our RIE efforts are closely integrated with the work of the Future Economy Council to support economic transformation and create more good jobs for Singaporeans.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We will scale up innovation platforms to drive S&T adoption across industry, and enhance the translation of research outcomes into globally-competitive and marketable S&T solutions that will derive greater value for Singapore and the world.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We will set up more of such platforms to meet emerging industry needs and better equip existing centres of innovation to support our enterprises to adopt new technologies.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We will continue to support the growth of more innovative Singapore-based companies and strengthen research-industry linkages through initiatives such as technology consortia and corporate laboratories, and strengthen access to talent, partners, and markets.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: In a post-COVID-19 world, we will also support industries to harness our S&T strengths more effectively to create new avenues of enterprise growth.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: For example, we initiated the Maritime Transformation Programme and the Aviation Transformation Programme to further Singapore’s position as a maritime and aviation hub.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: These initiatives leverage technologies such as big-data analytics and advanced sensors and communications to enhance our connectivity capabilities, and will enable Singapore to remain a critical transport and logistics node in a post-COVID-19 world where resilience and reliability will be more valued.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: As the pace of digitalisation continues to accelerate across the economy and society, we will also build on our investments in digital and automation technologies including artificial intelligence and robotics, which are critical enablers in Singapore's journey as a Smart Nation.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: In addition, we will continue to encourage more young Singaporeans to pursue good jobs and careers built around S&T.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: NRF will support the SGUnited Traineeship Programme, and offer traineeships in our R&D laboratories, deep-tech start-ups, accelerators and incubators.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: These experiences will be part of a broader effort to grow the RIE talent pool and strengthen people linkages within the RIE ecosystem.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Beyond Singapore's economic transformation, our RIE plan will continue to support national needs and improve the lives of Singaporeans.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: For example, we will partner the Ministry of Health to build on our R&D strengths in areas such as preventive care and digital healthcare to transform our healthcare system and deliver quality services at sustainable costs, and enable Singaporeans to lead healthy and productive lives.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We will also harness S&T to build on our capabilities in sustainable urban solutions and low-carbon technologies.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: This will contribute to our national efforts to address climate change, and enhance the quality of living in Singapore.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: As technology continues to accelerate the pace of change across society, we must continue to grow new S&T capabilities to meet future needs.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: NRF will continue to invest in building a robust base of research scientists and engineers, with strong links to the global community.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We will also refresh our strategic investments in major research centres across our universities and in the Agency for Science, Technology and Research, and build on our collaborations with international partners through our Campus for Research Excellence and Technology Enterprise.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: To further position Singapore as a global node of scientific excellence, we will build on our NRF Fellowships and Investigatorship schemes to attract both promising young scientists and established experts to pursue ground-breaking research in Singapore.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: This will enable Singapore to remain competitive and relevant to the world, as a vibrant Global-Asia node of technology, innovation, and enterprise.
